name: Botulax / Hutox / Meditoxin
lead: Botulax, Hutox and Meditoxin are botulinum toxin type A products made in South Korea. Botulax contains letibotulinumtoxinA, and Meditoxin (also marketed as Neuronox) was developed by Medy-Tox.[1][2][3] People seek them, mostly from licensed clinicians, to soften frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet and to slim a square or heavy jaw by relaxing the masseter muscle.[3][4][5]

The appearance payoff is the same as with other type A toxins. A toxin injected into a muscle blocks the nerve signal that makes it contract, so the skin above it creases less, and a masseter that is used less gradually shrinks, which narrows the lower face.[13][4] Korean brands are widely used across Asia, where jaw slimming and wrinkle treatment are common cosmetic procedures.[2]

Randomized trials have compared Meditoxin and Botulax with Botox in blepharospasm, post-stroke spasticity and cerebral palsy, and registered trials cover glabellar lines, crow's feet and masseteric hypertrophy.[3][5][6][8][9][10] Reviews comparing Asian formulations note that data on purity and immunogenicity for these newer products are more limited than for the original brands.[1][2]
infobox: letibotulinumtoxinA; US brand Letybo approved February 2024 for glabellar lines[14]
Prescription-only in US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia[13]

paras: Cosmetic uses of botulinum toxin type A center on the upper face. Injections into the muscles under the glabellar lines (between the brows), forehead and outer eye corners relax them so the overlying skin smooths.[13] Registered head-to-head trials of Botulax versus Botox covered glabellar lines (n=262) and crow's feet (n=240).[8][9] A further registered study compared letibotulinumtoxinA with other products for forehead wrinkles and how far each diffused.[15]

Botulinum toxin injected into the masseter reduces its bulk over weeks, which proponents use to soften a wide, square jawline. A phase II randomized trial of 80 adults in Asia with benign masseteric hypertrophy tested different Botulax doses for the cosmetic outcome.[16][10] A study using Meditoxin in 40 people followed chewing function over 12 weeks after injections into the masseter alone or masseter plus temporalis, as objective and subjective chewing tests were tracked.[4] Botulax has also been tested in a randomized trial for trapezius hypertrophy in women, where the trapezius area decreased at 12 weeks in both dose groups.[17] Botulinum toxin products in general are noted to reduce chewing power for solid foods when the masseter is injected.[13]

The Korean products were first studied in neurological conditions. Meditoxin was compared with Botox in essential blepharospasm in a double-blind trial, with improvement in spasm severity in 90.3 percent versus 86.2 percent and adverse effects in 16.1 percent versus 27.6 percent, without serious events.[3] Botulax was compared with Botox in a phase III trial in 187 people with post-stroke upper limb spasticity, and in 144 children with cerebral palsy and equinus foot deformity, where responder rates were 60.3 and 61.4 percent at 12 weeks.[5][6] A pilot study in eight people examined Botulax in chronic occipital neuralgia.[7] Other registered trials cover cervical dystonia, overactive bladder and temporomandibular myofascial pain.[18][19][20]

Reviewers note that all protein therapeutics are potentially immunogenic, that the amount of protein per unit matters, and that formulation data are not always public.[1][2] A 2020 review states that clinical evidence on the purity and immunogenicity of Nabota, Meditoxin/Neuronox and Botulax is limited.[1] Network meta-analyses of cerebral palsy trials have ranked Neuronox alongside other type A products on motor-function scores.[21]

Medy-Tox, a Korean company, developed Meditoxin (Neuronox) and Botulax was developed in Korea and tested in phase III trials from 2011 onward.[8][22] letibotulinumtoxinA received US approval under the brand Letybo in February 2024 for moderate-to-severe glabellar lines, on the basis of three trials (BLESS I to III) with 1,271 participants at sites in the US and European Union.[14] The most common side effects there were headache, drooping of the eyelid and brow, and eyelid twitching.[14] In 2008 and 2009 the FDA added boxed warnings to botulinum toxins about spread from the injection site, and the products are prescription-only in the US, UK, EU, Canada and Australia.[13] No published trials of Hutox were found.

For the class, cosmetic injections can cause bruising at the injection site, headache, flu-like symptoms, allergic reactions, and unintended weakness of nearby muscles if the toxin spreads.[13] In masseter treatment, reduced chewing strength is described.[13][4] In the Korean comparative trials, adverse events were generally similar between the Korean product and Botox and mostly mild.[3][5][6]

Randomized non-inferiority trials show Meditoxin and Botulax performing similarly to Botox in blepharospasm, post-stroke spasticity and pediatric cerebral palsy.[3][5][6] A 2018 American Academy of Ophthalmology review of toxins for facial dystonia included 1,523 patients across 13 studies, with pretarsal injections reaching higher response rates than preseptal injections (96 versus 86 percent).[23] For cosmetic uses, a phase II masseter trial, a trapezius trial and registered phase III trials in glabellar lines and crow's feet are described above.[16][17][8][9] Long-term blepharospasm follow-up with botulinum toxin A has also been published.[24]

card.summary: Korean botulinum toxin brands used abroad for wrinkles and jaw slimming, with trials mostly against Botox.
card.note: Prescription-only; reviews call evidence on purity and immunogenicity limited.

quick.overview:
These are Korean botulinum toxin A brands. Botulax is letibotulinumtoxinA and Meditoxin comes from Medy-Tox. Trials compare them with Botox.

Hutox has no studies in the material reviewed.
quick.mechanism: Type A toxins block acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, relaxing injected muscle.
quick.risks: Reviews note that any foreign protein can provoke immune reactions and that data on newer formulations are limited. All are prescription injectables.

chain: Wrinkle lines soften and an enlarged masseter gradually slims
Smoother forehead, eye area and a narrower lower face
angle.text: Like other botulinum toxin A products, these brands are used to relax the muscles that crease the skin between the brows, around the eyes and across the forehead, and to reduce bulky masseter muscles that widen the lower face. Trials have compared Botulax directly with Botox for frown lines, crow's feet and masseter hypertrophy.
